research:
## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the first print of the September 2026 change in BLS total nonfarm payrolls (FRED PAYEMS, month-over-month change). BLS publishes it in the Employment Situation release, scheduled for Friday 2026-10-02 at 8:30 a.m. ET. [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.htm?hl=en-GB)
- 2026-09-04: The latest release (August data) showed total nonfarm payrolls up 162,000, with unemployment unchanged at 4.1%. [BLS archive](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_09042026.htm) | [BLS TED](https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/payroll-employment-rose-162000-in-august-2026.htm). I could not open the BLS pages directly because the proxy refused the connection. The figures above come from search snippets and news coverage.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The September data comes out on 2026-10-02, after forecasts close.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-10: First Trust said the benchmark revisions "fall back in line." By sector, construction was revised up 62k and information up 87k, while manufacturing was revised down 67k and trade/transportation/utilities down 98k. [First Trust](https://www.ftportfolios.com/Commentary/EconomicResearch/2026/9/10/bls-payroll-revisions-fall-back-in-line-down-just-79,000)
- 2026-09-04: August came in at +162k, against consensus of roughly 53k (Dow Jones), 56k (LSEG) or 65k (FactSet).
  - Revisions: July went from -23k to +21k. Fox put the combined June and July revision at +55k. One snippet said June was "revised upwards, adding 31,000"; it is unclear whether that is the size of the revision or the new level.
  - Sectors: food services and bars added 59k and local government education added 42k, which largely reversed July's school-job losses. Information lost jobs. Wages were up 3.1% from a year earlier.
  - Commentary: Glassdoor's Daniel Zhao described "whiplash" from reports that alternate between good and bad. CNN listed headwinds including AI adoption, higher oil prices, policy uncertainty and the war with Iran. The FOMC meets September 16-17.
  - Sources: [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/09/04/nx-s1-5955549/august-job-numbers-far-exceed-economists-expectations) | [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/us-jobs-report-august-2026) | [CBS](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/august-jobs-report-us-labor-market/) | [CNBC preview](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/03/august-2026-jobs-report-payrolls.html)
- 2026-08-28: The preliminary benchmark revision for March 2026 was -79k for total nonfarm and -178k for private. That is the smallest since 2021; last year's preliminary revision was about -911k. The final benchmark arrives in February 2027 and does not affect the September first print. [BLS](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/prebmk_08282026.htm) | [Econoday](https://www.econoday.com/?p=16941)
- 2026-08-07: July's first print was -23k, against consensus of about 80k. Government fell 53k, with local government education down 50k, and private employers added 30k. May was revised from 129k to 63k and June from 57k to 20k. [First Trust](https://www.ftportfolios.com/Commentary/EconomicResearch/2026/8/7/nonfarm-payrolls-declined-23,000-in-july) | [Haver](https://www.haver.com/articles/u-s-payroll-employment-unexpectedly-declined-in-july)

## 4. Base rates
First prints for 2026:

| Month | First print | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Jan | +130k | Consensus 70k |
| Feb | -92k | Healthcare strike |
| Mar | +178k | |
| Apr | ~+115k | Single secondary source |
| May | +129k | |
| Jun | +57k | |
| Jul | -23k | |
| Aug | +162k | |

[Trading Economics](https://www.tradingeconomics.com/united-states/non-farm-payrolls/news/539119) | [TradingView](https://www.tradingview.com/symbols/ECONOMICS-USNFP/)

- Mean of the eight first prints: about +82k. Median: about +122k.
- Spread: about -90k to +180k, and month-to-month swings of 100k or more are common (May to Jul, Jul to Aug).
- Surprises against consensus were large: +60k to +118k in January, March and August, and about -100k to -150k in February and July.
- Revisions between first print and later estimates have run ±30-65k per month.
- Using the latest reported levels (June revised, July +21k, August +162k), the June-August average is roughly +70-80k. Underlying private hiring looks modest; private payrolls were about +30k per month in June and July.
- Seasonal note: September first prints often absorb noise from education seasonal adjustment. The August local-education rebound (+42k) could partly reverse.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Kalshi, Polymarket, Manifold or economist consensus for September 2026 payrolls that was clearly dated on or before 2026-09-11. Kalshi runs a market under ticker KXPAYROLLS-26SEP, but none of the snapshots I found was reliably dated before the cutoff.
- The usual consensus surveys (Dow Jones, Reuters, Bloomberg) typically appear in the last week before the release.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-09-16/17: FOMC meeting.
- Weekly jobless claims every Thursday. The claims survey week for the September payroll reference period includes September 12.
- About 2026-09-30: ADP report and JOLTS (August data).
- About 2026-10-01: ISM manufacturing employment index.
- 2026-10-02: BLS Employment Situation for September, which settles the question.
- Risks: the Iran war and higher oil prices, AI-related cuts in the information sector, volatility in government and education seasonal adjustment, and any strikes or weather events during the reference week.
